notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for Private VPC deployment. Primary ask: turnkey private connectivity + strong audit/KMS guarantees. Customer is security-first MSP serving regulated customers; can't accept transit through public internet for inference traffic. Prefers model pinning and private endpoints.

From AE call (10/21): 'We need the inference control plane to have zero public egress — all calls must terminate inside our account or via PrivateLink.' Wants ability to rotate CMKs and see CloudTrail events in our own SIEM. Concerned about IP exposure from egress LB.

Network preferences discussed: prefer AWS PrivateLink endpoint services over simple VPC peering due to cross-account isolation and easier access controls. For multi-VPC architecture they expect Transit Gateway for scale but only if PrivateLink is used for Redwood control-plane. Asked about route table exposure: wants no route table entries pointing to Redwood-managed subnets.

KMS: must be customer-managed key (CMK) with cross-account grants and key rotation policy. Interested in HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) for highest tier.

Audit logging: CloudTrail to customer S3 in their account + Kinesis Firehose integration to their SIEM. Logs must include request metadata (token_id, model_id, route) and be retained 7 years for regs.

Network security specifics they asked for: PrivateLink endpoint service with endpoint policies restricting principal accounts; explicit VPC endpoint policies; strict security group egress allowlist (443 only to Redwood PrivateLink IPs); NACLs default deny with minimal ephemeral ports allowed; no NAT gateways exposing public IPs for inference. Egress controls: allowlist outbound destinations, use of egress proxy for approved domains, strict TLS + mutual-TLS option for backend connections. IP allowlists: central static prefix lists managed in their account; Redwood to provide stable set of service prefixes (or support AWS Prefix List integration).

Operational asks: onboarding runbook, terraform modules for creating interface endpoints and endpoint service, CloudFormation examples, KMS grant playbook, and a predefined SOC2/ISO27001 evidence pack.

Quote from security lead: 'We will not sign until KMS behavior is crystal — who owns keys, how are grants issued, audit of decrypt ops.'

requirements_summary: Workload: embeddings + document search + internal support chat. Latency target: tail p95 < 250ms for embeddings; throughput: 500 concurrent embedding requests. Cost sensitivity: mid-high; will trade cost for strict residency and audit. Model pref: vetted open models + ability to pin versions. Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant in same VPC. Data residency: primary eu-west-1 for EU customers, NA for NA accounts. Audit/KMS: CMK required, CloudTrail delivered to customer's S3, HSM optional.
network_security_notes: Recommended pattern: expose Redwood inference via AWS PrivateLink endpoint service in Redwood AWS account; customer creates interface endpoints in their VPC pointing to service. Advantages called out: no route-table exposure, endpoint policies, VPC endpoint DNS override. For customers with many VPCs use Transit Gateway + centralized interface endpoints in shared-services VPC or deploy endpoint services per account. Must document non-transitive limitation of peering and recommend TGW for large fleets. Provide example security group rules: allow outbound 443 to specific endpoint ENIs + SG referencing allowed CIDRs; recommend endpoint policies limiting principal; show terraform sample. Egress controls: enforce egress via proxy/bastion, block 0.0.0.0/0 for inference subnets, use prefix-lists for allowed destinations. IP allowlists: maintain a published stable prefix-list and support automated updates via push and IAM role for customer's account to read list. Include emergency fallback: mutually authenticated TLS over PrivateLink for additional defense.
